solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Problem with one prisoner is point of no return (7)

blocks.note: the rub = the problem, as in Hamlet's 'there's the rub'

annotation.surface: A jailbird's trouble has reached a stage where there is no going back.
annotation.walkthrough: Caesar crossed the river Rubicon into Italy with his army, an act that made civil war certain.
annotation.definitionFit: To cross the Rubicon is to pass a point after which retreat is impossible.

entries.clue: House that is free around the centre of Marrakech (4)

indicators.note: RID wraps round the letter
take the middle letter of the word

blocks.note: fifth of the nine letters of MARRAKECH

annotation.surface: A house in Morocco that you can stay in for nothing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'That is' looks like it should abbreviate to IE; here it just links. Marrakech is well chosen, since a riad is a Moroccan townhouse.
annotation.definitionFit: A riad is a traditional Moroccan house built round an inner courtyard.

entries.clue: Criminal’s endless desire to be involved in endless clamour (7)

indicators.note: a word without end has lost its final letter
the first piece goes inside the second
a word without end has lost its final letter

blocks.note: blare = loud noise; endless drops the E to leave BLAR
an urge = a desire; endless drops the E to leave URG, which goes inside B…LAR

annotation.surface: A crook's unending longing to be caught up in constant noise.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay. Both pieces lose a final E before one sits inside the other.
annotation.definitionFit: A burglar is a criminal who breaks into buildings to steal.

entries.clue: Sound of train made by bird captured on tape (5)

indicators.note: a recording is something you hear played back

blocks.note: the chough is a red-billed crow

annotation.surface: Someone records a bird that mimics a steam train.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Made by bird' makes it look as if the bird makes the noise; the bird is only the word you hear. A chough is a crow of cliffs and coasts.
annotation.definitionFit: Chuff is the puffing sound of a steam engine.

entries.clue: Extremely sharp, odd taste in middle of fruitcake (8)

indicators.note: odd = strange, so the letters are rearranged
the middle of a word is its central letter, here the fifth of nine

blocks.note: fifth of the nine letters of FRUITCAKE

annotation.surface: A fruitcake whose centre tastes oddly tangy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' is part of the fodder, not a container signal. 'Sharp' here is the dressing sense: smart, as in a sharp suit.
annotation.definitionFit: Natty means smartly dressed, so the nattiest is the sharpest in that sense.

entries.clue: Fancy ring given to artist (7)

annotation.surface: An elaborate ring presented to a painter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' looks like an adjective describing the ring; it is a noun, a flight of imagination.
annotation.definitionFit: A chimera is an illusion or wild fancy, from the fire-breathing monster of myth.

entries.clue: Gentle touch provides safekeeping and, finally, happiness (6)

indicators.note: finally = at the end, so the word's end letter

blocks.note: to care for something is to keep it safe

annotation.surface: A tender touch gives security and, in the end, joy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Provides' looks like the link after the definition; it belongs to the wordplay, with 'safekeeping' to give CARES.
annotation.definitionFit: A caress is a light, affectionate stroke.

entries.clue: Italian team has to contend with series of probing questions? (9)

annotation.surface: An Italian football club faces a grilling from the press.
annotation.walkthrough: Inter Milan is the Milan club known by its first word.
annotation.definitionFit: An interview is a set of searching questions put to someone.

entries.clue: Royal princess from Europe with spirit (7)

blocks.note: a genie is a spirit of Arabian legend

annotation.surface: A lively princess from the Continent.
annotation.walkthrough: Princess Eugenie is a granddaughter of Queen Elizabeth II, daughter of Prince Andrew.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Eugenie, daughter of Prince Andrew, is one of the British royal family's princesses.

entries.clue: Prepared a little bit, ultimately only to protect that place (2,3,5)

indicators.note: ultimately = in the end, so the word's end letter
the outer word guards what goes inside it

blocks.note: there = that place, going inside AT…AD

annotation.surface: A cautious soldier gets a little ready, only to guard a position.
annotation.walkthrough: The comma splits the phrase oddly: 'a little bit' is A TAD, and 'ultimately' belongs to 'only', not to 'bit'.
annotation.definitionFit: At the ready means prepared for immediate use.

entries.clue: An unreal performance by Strummer? (3,6)

blocks.note: a performance with nothing real in it: miming
looks like Joe Strummer of The Clash; means anyone who strums

annotation.surface: A fake show put on by the Clash's frontman.
annotation.walkthrough: Joe Strummer was The Clash's singer and guitarist; the capital hides the plain sense, one who strums, and the guitar strummed is imaginary.
annotation.definitionFit: Air guitar is miming guitar playing with no instrument at all.

entries.clue: Drunk / not willing to buy everyone drinks? (5)

annotation.definition2: not willing to buy everyone drinks?

blocks.note: drunk as in tipsy, the slang sense

blocks.clueFragment: not willing to buy everyone drinks?
blocks.note: stingy, never standing a round in the pub

annotation.surface: A tipsy pub-goer who won't stand a round.
annotation.walkthrough: Buying everyone drinks is standing a round, a British pub custom; the question mark marks the stingy sense as an example.
annotation.definitionFit: Tight means both drunk and mean with money.

entries.clue: Crazy finance rules surrounding current protection product (4,9)

indicators.note: crazy = mixed up, so the letters are rearranged
the rearranged letters go round the I

annotation.surface: A complaint that regulations on money make no sense.
annotation.walkthrough: The I sits inside the rearranged letters, so it counts in the anagram's letter total.
annotation.definitionFit: Life insurance is a financial product protecting dependants against a death.

entries.clue: Hit penned by gross, boorish Aussie musician in the 70s? (4,6)

indicators.note: penned = enclosed, so LAM sits inside GR

blocks.note: an ocker is an uncouth Australian man

annotation.surface: A crude Australian singer's chart-topper from the seventies.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hit' wants to be a chart hit, and 'penned' a song written; hit is a blow and penned means enclosed.
annotation.definitionFit: Glam rock, with its glitter and platform boots, belonged to the early 1970s.

entries.clue: Is Cyril Scott finally recollected as a writer of music? (8)

indicators.note: finally = at the end, so the word's end letter
re-collected = gathered again in a new order

annotation.surface: Is the composer Cyril Scott at last remembered as a musician?
annotation.walkthrough: Cyril Scott was an English composer; the question mark admits that a lyricist writes the words for music, not the notes.
annotation.definitionFit: A lyricist writes song words, so writes for music rather than the music itself.

entries.clue: Certain hormone is implicated in my mood (9)

indicators.note: implicated = folded in, so IS goes inside TONE

blocks.note: cor and my are both exclamations of surprise
tone = mood, as in the tone of a meeting
used as it stands, inside TONE

annotation.surface: A claim that a particular hormone drives the writer's moods.
annotation.walkthrough: 'My' is the exclamation, like 'my, my!', and cor is its British equivalent; it is not a possessive.
annotation.definitionFit: Cortisone is a steroid hormone of the adrenal gland.

entries.clue: I happen to be drawn in by whisky and choice steak (3,3)

indicators.note: the outer word takes in what goes before

annotation.surface: A diner is lured in by a promise of whisky and a fine steak.
annotation.walkthrough: RYE opens to take in I BE.
annotation.definitionFit: Rib-eye is a prime cut of beef from the rib section.

entries.clue: Prison time accepted by Wimbledon champ (8)

indicators.note: taken into the other word

annotation.surface: A tennis champion does time behind bars.
annotation.walkthrough: Carlos Alcaraz, the Spanish tennis player, won Wimbledon in 2023 and 2024.
annotation.definitionFit: Alcatraz was the notorious prison on an island in San Francisco Bay.

entries.clue: Cheapskate has yen for being unhappy (6)

annotation.surface: A skinflint longs to be sad.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Yen' wants to mean a longing, which suits the surface; it is the currency.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: misery is deep unhappiness, and 'being unhappy' names that state as a noun phrase.

entries.clue: Relative in position to take on parental duties primarily (7)

indicators.note: the outer word takes the letters inside it
primarily = in the first place, so each word's first letter

blocks.note: stead = place, as in 'in his stead'
first letters of PARENTAL DUTIES, going inside STE…AD

annotation.surface: A relation steps in to take over the parenting.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is almost a definition in itself: a stepdad does take on a parent's duties.
annotation.definitionFit: A stepdad is a relative by marriage, a mother's husband.

entries.clue: Bragger’s way of dealing with birthday candles? (8)

annotation.definition2: way of dealing with birthday candles?

blocks.clueFragment: way of dealing with birthday candles?
blocks.note: read as two words: how you get every candle out in one breath

annotation.surface: A boaster's method of putting out the candles on a cake.
annotation.walkthrough: The second sense splits as two words, BLOW HARD, which the question mark signals.
annotation.definitionFit: A blowhard is a boastful, blustering person.

entries.clue: Tune left for John Lennon, for example (7)

annotation.surface: A song Lennon left behind.
annotation.walkthrough: Liverpool's airport is named Liverpool John Lennon Airport, so the Beatle stands for the place.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Liverpool named its airport after the Beatle, so John Lennon is one airport.

entries.clue: In a state of shock? That’s funny, in a good way (6)

indicators.note: HA goes inside the letters that follow

blocks.note: ha! = the response to a joke

annotation.surface: Someone is startled, then decides it was funny after all.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In a good way' reads as a phrase meaning pleasantly; it is A, G and ST with HA placed in.
annotation.definitionFit: Aghast means filled with shock and horror.

entries.clue: At first, total beginner worked with a top, top cricketer? (7,6)

indicators.note: at first = at the start, so the word's opening letter
worked = kneaded into new shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, used as it stands

annotation.surface: A complete novice at cricket practises with a spinning top.
annotation.walkthrough: The doubled 'top' hides the join: the first is fodder, the second is the definition. An opener bats first, at the top of the order.
annotation.definitionFit: An opening batter goes in first, at the top of cricket's batting order.

entries.clue: Electronic piloting system acquired by Delta, cannily (5)

indicators.note: the answer is held within the words that follow

annotation.surface: An airline shrewdly buys a new flight navigation system.
annotation.walkthrough: Delta, the American airline, suits the surface; the answer spans its end and the start of the next word.
annotation.definitionFit: TACAN, tactical air navigation, is a radio navigation system for aircraft.

entries.clue: A member of the family producing jumble sale sign? (2,2)

annotation.surface: A relative makes a sign for a charity sale.
annotation.walkthrough: A jumble sale is a British charity sale of second-hand goods, which are sold as they are.
annotation.definitionFit: Goods sold 'as is' come with no promise about their condition.

entries.clue: Quirky, picky, periodically retiring little ’un (5)

indicators.note: take letters at regular intervals
retiring = drawing back, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: second and fourth letters of PICKY

annotation.surface: A strange, fussy, shy little child.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Retiring' looks like part of the child's shy character; it means drawing back, so the joined pieces read backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: Kiddo is an informal word for a child, a little one.

entries.clue: Terrible, terrible actors bearing evidence of debt (9)

indicators.note: terrible = badly done, so the letters are rearranged
carrying the next piece inside

blocks.note: an IOU is a written promise to pay, going inside ATROC…S

annotation.surface: A dreadful company of players carrying proof of what they owe.
annotation.walkthrough: The repeated 'terrible' is split: the first is the definition, the second tells you to rearrange ACTORS.
annotation.definitionFit: Atrocious means extremely bad.

entries.clue: After starters of really excellent duck medallions, have lamb, perhaps (3,4)

indicators.note: the second piece follows the first
starters are what begin things, here the opening letters of each word

blocks.clueFragment: starters of really excellent duck medallions
blocks.note: first letters of REALLY EXCELLENT DUCK MEDALLIONS
to have a meal = to eat it

annotation.surface: A diner starts with duck medallions and then has the lamb.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a menu, and 'starters' as first courses; here they are initial letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Lamb is classed as red meat, along with beef and pork.

entries.clue: Japanese school getting hot in its most elevated points (7)

indicators.note: H is put in ITS, as a thing is placed in a box

blocks.note: Zen, the Japanese school of Buddhism

annotation.surface: A Japanese school heats up in its highest parts.
annotation.walkthrough: 'School' suggests a place of lessons; it is a school of thought.
annotation.definitionFit: A zenith is a highest point, originally the point in the sky directly overhead.
